doc.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Father's success story, wine, and Tommy Dorsey at the Hotel Sherman
summary: His father lived to see their success; Sy Oliver and Dorsey loved his father's wine when the band played Chicago.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And he got to see some of your really good success.
Oh great, so he saw you with—

He saw us both having some nice things and seeing us do what he had in mind all through. He was a wonderful guy. I remember I took Ziggy Elman’s place, that was the Herd just before he went in the service, and I took his place with Tommy Dorsey’s band, and Sy Oliver was writing for the band. And at the Hotel Sherman they changed the band every two weeks, another name band would come in. And he knew my father, and he would say, “Tony, did you bring some wine with you?” Because he loved my father’s wine. My father had a wine cellar with bottles that, as I remember them, 25 years they’d been — and every time he went to Chicago he said, “Your Dad coming in, Pete?” I’d say, “Yeah.” So it was quite something.
